name: Vic Cho
life: Vic collects sounds at a volume that lets the people producing them hear each other. Some of the best recordings in the cupboard have no permission form. They will stay in the cupboard. Wednesday often includes a stop at the blocks below Foundry Lofts, where Vic checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I recorded the crunch for a midnight program and accidentally caught two men making up in the background. I asked them which part I could keep. They chose the silence after it.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a gray fisher's sweater and a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. Vic has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, with a loose dark braid. Vic folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing during a conversation.
personality: Vic admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Vic learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To give the recorded couple a final choice about the broadcast.
family: Franklin Sun is Vic’s second cousin. Vic saves a place. Franklin chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The ladder crossing*, Franklin says, “I saw the ladder's shadow stretch across my old playground and asked for a photograph.”
connections: Eli Carr. A night broadcast and two music tickets link the bakery's sounds to an audience beyond the block.
